Feet have thicker skin than the rest of the body and few oil glands, so they are often the first place to feel dry, especially in winter, when boots, tights and central heating all take their toll. A good foot cream, used regularly, keeps heels and soles feeling soft and comfortable. Here is how to choose one, and how to fit it into a simple at-home pedicure.

Why feet get so dry

The skin on your heels and soles takes your weight all day. It is naturally thick, and when it dries out it can feel rough and tight. Hot baths, long showers, walking barefoot on hard floors and closed shoes in heated rooms all make it drier. Moisturising little and often works better than an occasional rescue.

Foot cream or foot butter?

  • A foot cream contains water as well as oils and butters, so it sinks in quickly. It suits daily use, morning or night.
  • A foot butter or balm has no water: it is a solid blend of oils, butters and wax that sits on the skin for longer. It suits very dry heels and works well at night under cotton socks.

Foot cream: Vilvah Foot Care Cream

Vilvah Foot Care Cream (£16, 100ml) is a rich cream with four butters (shea, avocado, mango and cocoa), sunflower, argan and kalonji (black seed) oils, glycerine and a little peppermint oil for a cool, fresh scent. Massage it into clean, dry feet, ideally before bed. It also comes as the Vilvah Foot Cream & Body Lotion Kit (£37.99), paired with the Milk Body Lotion (oat milk, ceramide, olive squalane and jojoba oil) for the rest of the body.

Foot butter: Deyga Foot Butter

Deyga Foot Butter (£12.99, 40g) is a short-ingredient balm: virgin coconut oil, olive oil, refined beeswax, vitamin E and vanilla essential oil. Warm a little between your fingers and work it into heels, soles and toes. For a richer finish, put it on at night and slip on cotton socks. It contains beeswax, so it is not vegan.

Already have a favourite body butter? A rich one such as Deyga Rose & Geranium Body Butter (£15.99) works on feet too; our body butter guide explains how to use it.

A simple at-home pedicure

  1. Soak. Dissolve two spoonfuls of Deyga Foot Soak Powder (£16.99, 160g) in a bowl of warm water. It blends sea salt and Himalayan pink salt with rose, lemon and peppermint oil. Soak for 10 to 15 minutes, no longer.
  2. Scrub. Massage Deyga Foot Scrub (£17.99, 100g) over damp feet in slow circles, focusing on the heels. Granulated sugar gives it a gentle grit, in coconut and almond oils with shea butter. Rinse with warm water. Once or twice a week is enough.
  3. Dry well, especially between the toes.
  4. Moisturise with foot cream or foot butter, then put on clean cotton socks if it is bedtime.

The Deyga Mini Foot Spa Combo (£35.99) puts the soak, the scrub and the foot butter in one box, which also makes an easy Christmas present. A natural Deyga Organic Loofah (£12.99) is handy for a quick buff of the heels in the shower. For scrubs for the rest of the body, see our body scrub guide.

Everyday habits for comfortable feet

  • Moisturise daily, ideally after a bath or shower, while skin is still slightly damp.
  • Keep showers warm, not hot, and do not leave feet soaking for long.
  • Wear socks around the house in winter rather than walking barefoot on cold, hard floors.
  • Do not use foot cream between the toes; keep that skin dry.

Good to know

  • Patch test before first use: the cream, butter and soak all contain essential oils, and the scrub contains almond oil.
  • Do not scrub broken or sore skin.
  • If you have diabetes or poor circulation, ask your GP or a podiatrist before soaking or scrubbing your feet.
  • Painful, deep or bleeding cracks in the heels, or any change you are unsure about, are worth showing to a pharmacist, your GP or a podiatrist.

A mini perfume set is a box of small bottles, usually 4ml to 15ml each, from one perfume house. Why choose a mini perfume set?

  • As a gift when you are not sure of their taste: several scents from a house they like is a safer bet than one full bottle.

Sizes vary from set to set, so check the millilitres as well as the number of bottles.

Goat milk soap is a bar soap made with goat milk in its recipe. It gives a creamy lather and leaves skin feeling soft rather than tight, which is why many people keep a bar by the bath or basin. This guide explains how goat milk soap is made, how to use it on your face and body, and how to choose between the goat milk soaps from Vilvah, one of the two Indian natural brands Swansura is an official UK partner of.

What is goat milk soap?

Every true bar soap is made by mixing oils or butters with lye (sodium hydroxide). The two react together to form soap, a process called saponification. In goat milk soap, fresh goat milk goes into the recipe, which gives the bar a creamy lather. You will see sodium hydroxide at the end of the ingredient lists below: that is how all bar soap is made.

Vilvah makes its goat milk bars by hand with farm-fresh goat milk and a base of plant oils such as extra virgin olive, coconut and castor oil. Coconut oil gives the bubbly lather, olive oil a gentle feel and castor oil a cushioned foam.

The Vilvah goat milk soaps

  • Classic Goat Milk Soap (£9.99, 115g): goat milk, olive, coconut and castor oils, lightly scented with lavender essential oil. Six ingredients in all, and listed as suiting dry and sensitive skin.
  • Classic Rose Goat Milk Soap (£9.99, 125g): goat milk with rose petals, rose hydrosol, French pink clay, shea butter and rice bran oil, scented with rose and geranium essential oils.
  • Charcoal Goat Milk Soap (£9.99, 115g): activated charcoal with goat milk, for a clean-feeling daily wash. The charcoal gives the bar its colour.

All three are in our goat milk soap collection. One bar that looks similar is not a goat milk soap: Vilvah’s Cucumber, Curd & Mint Soap (£9.99) is made with cucumber juice, curd and mint leaves, for a cool, zesty morning wash.

Which bar should you choose?

  • A soft, simple scent: the Classic bar, with lavender.
  • A floral scent: Classic Rose.
  • A clean-feeling wash: Charcoal.
  • Something fresh and minty: Cucumber, Curd & Mint.
  • A bar without milk: Deyga’s Shea Saffron Bath Bar (£15.99) and Rose Pink Clay Bath Bar (£14.99) are made with raw shea butter and coconut and olive oils.

How to use goat milk soap

  1. Wet your skin and the bar, then work up a lather between your hands.
  2. Massage the foam over damp face or body, keeping it away from your eyes.
  3. Rinse well with warm water and pat dry.
  4. Follow with a moisturiser or body lotion if your skin tends to feel dry.
  5. Keep the bar on a draining soap dish between uses. A handmade bar left sitting in water softens quickly.

The Classic, Classic Rose and Cucumber bars contain essential oils, so patch test before first use.

Goat milk shampoo and hair care

Goat milk is not only for soap. Vilvah Goat Milk Shampoo (£15.99, 250ml) is a creamy shampoo with goat milk, jasmine flower water and hydrolysed pea protein, with a light jasmine and citrus scent. Vilvah Goat Milk Hair Mask (£31.99) pairs goat milk with ceramides and argan oil to condition dry, frizzy lengths. Buy them together in the Goat Milk Hair Kit (£34.99), or try the shampoo with Vilvah’s Cream Conditioner in the Bestseller Hair Kit (£27.99). Our natural shampoo guide covers how to choose a shampoo for dry hair.

Goat milk for the body

The Vilvah Milk Body Kit (£44.99) pairs a Goat Milk Body Wash, made with goat milk, chamomile water and coconut oil and scented with vanilla, with a Milk Body Lotion. If you were looking for a goat milk body lotion, note that the Milk Body Lotion (£25.99) is made with oat milk, ceramide NP and olive squalane: the goat milk in this kit is in the body wash. For richer body care after a soap, read our body butter guide.

Good to know

  • Goat milk soap is not vegan, because it contains goat milk.
  • Every skin is different. If you have a skin condition, ask a pharmacist or GP before trying a new soap.
  • A goat milk bar wrapped in tissue makes an easy gift: see our stocking fillers and stocking fillers guide.
  • Everything is 100% authentic and shipped from the UK. Browse the whole goat milk range; UK delivery is free on orders over £40.

Oud is one of the most talked-about notes in perfume: deep, woody and a little smoky. Designer houses such as Tom Ford, Gucci, Guerlain and Chopard each have their own take on it. Here is what oud is, how the best-known oud perfumes differ, and how to choose and wear one.

What is oud?

Oud, also called agarwood or aoud, is a dark, fragrant resin that forms in the wood of agar (Aquilaria) trees. It has been treasured in the Middle East and South Asia for centuries, burned as incense and worn as an oil. Natural oud is rare, so many modern perfumes use an oud accord: a blend of woods, resins and leathery notes built to give the same rich effect. Gucci, for example, lists an oud accord in its base notes.

Tom Ford Oud Wood

Tom Ford Oud Wood Eau de Parfum (from £115.99, 30ml or 50ml) is the gentlest way into oud. Its key notes are oud wood, rosewood and cardamom over sandalwood, vetiver, tonka bean and amber, so the oud reads smooth and warm rather than smoky. It is unisex and easy to wear in the office or in the evening. See every Tom Ford fragrance, or read our Tom Ford perfume guide for Black Orchid, Noir Extreme and Neroli Portofino.

Gucci Intense Oud

Gucci Intense Oud Eau de Parfum (£73.99, 90ml) is darker. Black pepper and olibanum (frankincense) open it; amber woods, sandalwood and cedarwood sit at the heart; leather, patchouli, gurjun balsam and the oud accord form the base. Expect incense and leather more than sweetness. Shop all Gucci.

Tom Ford Oud Wood or Gucci Intense Oud?

  • Choose Oud Wood if you want a soft, creamy wood with a touch of spice that suits everyday wear.
  • Choose Intense Oud if you like incense, leather and a bolder, smokier trail for evenings and colder months.

Three more oud perfumes

  • Guerlain Oud Essentiel (£94.99, 125ml): saffron and pelargonium, then rose, oud and cedarwood over leather, frankincense and guaiac wood. A rose-and-leather oud, made unisex.
  • Chopard Oud Malaki (£48.99, 80ml): grapefruit, lavender and artemisia, then tobacco, spices and leather over oud, ambergris and dark woods. Made for men, and the most affordable oud in this guide.
  • Montale Aoud Damascus (£52.99, 100ml): damask rose, aoud and saffron with amber, woods and musk. Montale is known for rose and oud, and this one is made for women.

The Al Haramain Amber Oud editions

Al Haramain's Amber Oud range is a popular Arabian line, but read the notes: not every edition is built around oud. Our Amber Oud editions guide compares them all. Amber Oud White Edition (from £34.99) is bergamot and orange, then jasmine, rose and freesia over musk, vanilla and patchouli, and is listed for women. Amber Oud Carbon Edition (from £35.99) is a fresh, aromatic men's scent of lavender, rosemary, bergamot, sage and vetiver. Amber Oud Bleu Edition (from £38.99) is citrus and mint over incense, vetiver and sandalwood. For the Gold, Ruby, Tobacco and Black editions, and for Lattafa, read our guide to Arabian perfume and Lattafa Khamrah Qahwa.

Which oud perfume suits you?

  • New to oud: Tom Ford Oud Wood, or a fresher Amber Oud edition.
  • You love incense and leather: Gucci Intense Oud or Guerlain Oud Essentiel.
  • You love rose: Montale Aoud Damascus or Guerlain Oud Essentiel.
  • Warm and spicy: Chopard Oud Malaki.

Oud is traditionally unisex, so "for men" or "for women" on the label is only a starting point. Browse unisex perfume, perfume for men and perfume for women.

How to wear oud

  1. Start small: one or two sprays. Oud notes are rich, and a little goes a long way.
  2. Apply to moisturised skin on the wrists, neck or chest. Our guide to layering oud with body butter explains why.
  3. Let it settle: do not rub your wrists together. Oud perfumes often change a lot after the first half hour, so judge them later in the day.
  4. Test before you buy a full bottle if you can, or start with a smaller size.

Good to know

  • Eau de parfum is the most common strength for oud perfumes; read extrait vs eau de parfum for what the label means.
  • Patch test on your inner arm if you have sensitive skin, and keep perfume away from your eyes.
  • Store bottles away from heat and sunlight, with the cap on.

Shop every oud perfume, all Arabian perfume and niche perfume, all 100% authentic and dispatched from the UK.

When skin feels tight and dry, a body butter is the richest way to put comfort back. It is thicker than a lotion, melts on contact with warm skin and leaves a soft, cushioned finish. Here is how a body butter differs from a body lotion, which one suits your skin, and how to use it so a little goes a long way.

What is body butter?

A body butter is a thick, rich moisturiser for the body, made mainly from plant butters such as shea butter and cocoa butter. It feels firm in the jar, softens as it warms in your hands and leaves a soft, cushioned layer on the skin. A small amount covers a large area, so one jar lasts a good while.

Body butter vs body lotion: what is the difference?

The difference is mostly water. A body lotion is mainly water with some oils and butters, so it feels light, sinks in fast and suits everyday use. A body butter is made mostly or entirely of plant butters and oils, such as shea butter, cocoa butter and almond oil, so it is richer, takes a little longer to sink in and leaves skin feeling soft for longer. Body creams sit in between.

  • Choose a body butter for very dry or rough skin, for elbows, knees, shins and heels, at night, and in cold weather.
  • Choose a body lotion for a quick morning routine, for warm days, or if you dislike a rich finish.

Many people use both: a lotion in the morning and a butter at night.

Our body butters, compared

Chocolate body butter

Deyga Chocolate Body Butter (£15.99, 100g) is a short, simple blend: cocoa powder, shea butter, almond oil, jojoba oil, cocoa butter and vitamin E, with no water in the ingredient list. The cocoa gives it a light, natural chocolate scent rather than a sweet perfume, which makes this chocolate body butter a favourite for evenings and a lovely small gift.

Rose and geranium body butter

Deyga Rose & Geranium Body Butter (£15.99, 40g) swaps cocoa for floral essential oils: rose and geranium with shea butter, almond oil, jojoba oil and vitamin E. The 40g size is small enough for a handbag, for dry hands and elbows on the go.

A luxury body butter

Highborn London Natural Luminosity Body Butter (£50) comes in a large 220ml glass jar in recyclable packaging, free from parabens and sulphates. Its butter-soft formula is made to smooth over the whole body, and the brand says it can be used on the face too.

Body butter for dry skin: how to use it

  1. Apply after a shower or bath, while skin is still slightly damp. The butter seals in the water on your skin.
  2. Warm a small amount, about the size of a grape for each leg, between your palms until it softens.
  3. Press, then smooth it over the skin in long strokes, rather than rubbing hard.
  4. Add a little more to elbows, knees, shins and heels.
  5. Give it a few minutes to sink in before getting dressed. At night, it can work while you sleep.

Once or twice a week, use a scrub first, such as Vilvah Cookie N Cream Body Polish (£22.99) or Deyga Body Scrub (£16.99). On freshly smoothed skin, a body butter spreads further and feels more even. Browse all body scrubs.

Prefer something lighter? Body lotions for dry skin

If a butter feels too rich, a body lotion for dry skin gives you the same ingredients in a lighter texture:

  • Deyga Almond Milk Body Lotion (£14.99, 100ml): almond milk, cocoa butter, shea butter and almond oil with cucumber water. A good pick if you are looking for a cocoa butter body lotion that is quick to absorb.
  • Vilvah Milk Body Lotion (£25.99, 250ml): oat milk, ceramides, olive squalane, coconut and jojoba oils in a vegan formula, made for daily use.

See all body lotions for dry skin, or shop more for dry skin.

Feet and lips

Heels and lips are the driest places of all, and they have their own butters. Deyga Foot Butter (£12.99, 40g) blends virgin coconut oil, olive oil, beeswax, vitamin E and vanilla essential oil; apply it at night and pull on cotton socks. Our foot cream guide has a simple at-home pedicure. For lips, Highborn London Superior Lip Butter (£22.50) comes in a 15ml size, or a large 50ml. For the softest lips, use a scrub first: see how to use a lip scrub.

Body butter and perfume

Perfume lasts longer on moisturised skin, because there is something for it to hold on to. Smooth an unscented or lightly scented butter over your pulse points before you spray. We explain how in how to layer oud with body butter.

Good to know

  • Patch test first, especially with butters that contain essential oils, such as rose, geranium or vanilla.
  • Keep it cool. Natural butters soften in warm rooms and firm up in the cold; keep the jar out of direct sun and heat.
  • Not for broken or irritated skin. If your skin is very dry, cracked or itchy for a long time, speak to a pharmacist or your GP.
